forecasts.question: Will the Strait of Hormuz commercial vessel transit rate reach a 7-day average of 5 or more vessels per day at any point before EOD 2026-10-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Current Hormuz transit: approximately 1 vessel/day as of Aug 16 (UKMTO data; ~1.4% of pre-conflict 73/day baseline). War-risk insurance at 40× pre-crisis; 6 P&I clubs withdrew cover; UAE cut trade links with Iran Aug 19; ceasefire terminated. Getting from 1/day to ≥5/day (7-day avg) within 42 days requires either a security framework or a unilateral insurer decision to accept elevated risk — both are low-probability given the escalation trajectory. Threshold set at 5/day (vs. N4's 30/day) to reflect the realistic lower bound of functional, albeit minimal, commercial navigation.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch or equivalent AIS tracker (Windward, TankerMap) records a 7-day trailing average of ≥5 commercial vessel transits/day through the Hormuz chokepoint at any point before EOD 2026-10-01. Naval warships do NOT count.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escorts and warships do NOT count toward commercial threshold. One-off single-day spikes without a sustained 7-day average ≥5 = NO. Military-escorted commercial convoys count if the vessels themselves are commercial.
